title: Finite free Hopf duals and primitive-generator pairing criterion
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $B$ be an associative unital Hopf $R$-algebra, finite free as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with cocommutative comultiplication. Here Hopf means that its comultiplication and counit are unital algebra maps, coassociativity and the two counit identities hold, and its antipode $S$ satisfies $m(S\otimes1)\Delta=m(1\otimes S)\Delta=\eta\varepsilon$. Tensor products are over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $B^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,R)$ is a commutative Hopf $R$-algebra with $(fg)(b)=(f\otimes g)(\Delta_B b)$, unit $\varepsilon_B$, coproduct determined by $(\Delta f)(b\otimes b')=f(bb')$, counit $f\mapsto f(1)$ and antipode $f\mapsto f\circ S_B$. For every commutative $R$-algebra $T$, evaluation gives a Hopf algebra isomorphism $T\otimes_R B^\vee\simeq(T\otimes_R B)^\vee$, with $(t\otimes f)(t'\otimes b)=tt'f(b)$. Suppose in addition that $B$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by a set $P$ of primitive elements: $\Delta b=b\otimes1+1\otimes b$ and $\varepsilon_B(b)=0$ for $b\in P$. Let $C$ be any commutative Hopf $R$-algebra (not required finite or flat). Give $C^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,R)$ convolution multiplication $(a*a')(c)=(a\otimes a')(\Delta_Cc)$. For every unital $R$-algebra map $r:B\to C^*$, define its transpose $t_r:C\to B^\vee$ by $t_r(c)(b)=r(b)(c)$. Then $t_r$ is a Hopf algebra homomorphism if and only if for every $b\in P$ and $c,c'\in C$,
$$r(b)(cc')=\varepsilon_C(c)r(b)(c')+r(b)(c)\varepsilon_C(c').$$
Conversely every Hopf algebra map $t:C\to B^\vee$ has a unique such convolution-algebra transpose $r$. These correspondences are natural, and the displayed formulas commute with extension of scalars whenever the pairings are scalar extended.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, printed pp.222--223, finite-dual construction; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65--66. General finite-free base-ring pairing criterion extracted from the algebraic construction underlying Proposition 11.36, p.223; the criterion in this ring generality is agent-supplied, not a claim of a separately stated theorem in Milne.

proof.text: Put $A=B^\vee$. Choose a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $B$ as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and write $e_i^*(\sum_j a_je_j)=a_i$. Every $f\in A$ has the unique expansion $f=\sum_i f(e_i)e_i^*$, so $A$ is finite free. By [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra], applied to the coalgebra $B$ and algebra $R$, its convolution product is associative with unit $\varepsilon_B$. It is commutative because $\Delta_B$ is cocommutative: $(fg)(b)=(f\otimes g)(\Delta_B b)=(g\otimes f)(\Delta_B b)=(gf)(b)$. By [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual], transposing multiplication $m_B$ gives a unique linear map $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes A$ with $(\Delta_Af)(b,b')=f(bb')$. Define $\varepsilon_A(f)=f(1_B)$ and $S_A(f)=f\circ S_B$. Here evaluation of a tensor of functionals means the product of their values.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: The tensors $e_i\otimes e_j$ form a basis of $B\otimes B$: expand each factor, and apply the product functionals $e_i^*\otimes e_j^*$ to recover its coefficients. The same argument works for three factors. Thus [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual], iterated, permits testing identities in $A^{\otimes n}$ on $n$ elements of $B$ for $n=2,3$. Both iterated coproducts of $f$ evaluate at $(b,b',b'')$ as $f((bb')b'')=f(b(b'b''))$. Hence $\Delta_A$ is coassociative. The two counit composites evaluate at $b$ as $f(1_Bb)=f(b)=f(b1_B)$. This proves both counit identities.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: Write $\Delta_Bb=\sum b_1\otimes b_2$ and $\Delta_Bb'=\sum b'_1\otimes b'_2$; these denote arbitrary finite tensor presentations, not unique components. Since $\Delta_B$ is an algebra map, $\Delta_A(fg)$ evaluated at $(b,b')$ is $\sum f(b_1b'_1)g(b_2b'_2)$. This is also the evaluation of $(\Delta_Af)(\Delta_Ag)$, using the convolution product in each tensor factor. Injectivity in [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual] proves equality. Also $\Delta_A(1_A)(b,b')=\varepsilon_B(bb')=\varepsilon_B(b)\varepsilon_B(b')$, proving unit compatibility. Finally $\varepsilon_A(fg)=(fg)(1_B)=f(1_B)g(1_B)$ because $\Delta_B(1_B)=1_B\otimes1_B$, and $\varepsilon_A(1_A)=\varepsilon_B(1_B)=1_R$. Linearity supplies scalar compatibility. Thus $A$ is a commutative bialgebra.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: Evaluate $m_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A f$ at $b$. Its value is $\sum f(S_B(b_1)b_2)=f(\varepsilon_B(b)1_B)=\varepsilon_B(b)f(1_B)$ by the first antipode identity in $B$. Similarly $m_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A f$ evaluates as $\sum f(b_1S_B(b_2))=\varepsilon_B(b)f(1_B)$. These are exactly the values of $\eta_A\varepsilon_A(f)$, since $1_A=\varepsilon_B$. The evaluations are justified by the tensor-dual formula of [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual]. Both antipode identities follow; hence the stated operations make $A$ a commutative Hopf algebra.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: For any commutative $R$-algebra $T$, the scalar-extended Hopf operations are defined on pure tensors by extending the original linear maps, with $(t\otimes b)(u\otimes b')=tu\otimes bb'$ and $\Delta_{B_T}(t\otimes b)=\sum(t\otimes b_1)\otimes_T(1\otimes b_2)$. Each Hopf axiom on pure tensors is the scalar extension of that axiom for $B$; pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The family $(1\otimes e_i)$ is a $T$-basis, with coefficient maps $t\otimes b\mapsto t e_i^*(b)$, as the unique basis expansion in [def-weil-pbc-free-module] shows. The displayed evaluation map $\theta:T\otimes A\to(B_T)^\vee$ is therefore invertible, with inverse $h\mapsto\sum_i h(1\otimes e_i)\otimes e_i^*$. For the product, both $\theta((t\otimes f)(u\otimes g))$ and $\theta(t\otimes f)\theta(u\otimes g)$ take $v\otimes b$ to $tuv\sum f(b_1)g(b_2)$. For coproducts both sides evaluated at $(v\otimes b,w\otimes b')$ give $tvw f(bb')$; [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual] over $T$ detects equality. Unit, counit and antipode compatibility respectively give $v\varepsilon_B(b)$, $t f(1_B)$ and $tv f(S_Bb)$. Thus $\theta$ is a Hopf algebra isomorphism. No flatness of $T$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra] to $C$ and $R$; it supplies the convolution algebra $C^*$ even when $C$ is neither finite nor flat. Transposing the bilinear pairing $\langle b,c\rangle=r(b)(c)$ gives the linear map $t=t_r$. Because $r$ is a unital algebra map,
$$\langle bb',c\rangle=\sum\langle b,c_1\rangle\langle b',c_2\rangle,\qquad \langle1_B,c\rangle=\varepsilon_C(c).$$
Consequently $\Delta_A(t(c))=(t\otimes t)\Delta_Cc$: their evaluations at $(b,b')$ are respectively the two sides of the first identity, and [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual] detects equality. The second identity gives $\varepsilon_A(t(c))=\varepsilon_C(c)$. Thus $t$ is already a counital coalgebra map, without the primitive condition.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: Assume the displayed primitive-generator condition. Substituting $c=c'=1_C$ gives $\langle p,1_C\rangle=2\langle p,1_C\rangle$, so $\langle p,1_C\rangle=0$ by subtraction, over any $R$. Since $\Delta_C1_C=1_C\otimes1_C$, evaluation at $1_C$ is an algebra map from the convolution algebra $C^*$ to $R$. Hence $b\mapsto\langle b,1_C\rangle$ is an algebra map. It agrees with $\varepsilon_B$ on $P$ and on scalars; multiplicativity gives agreement on every word in $P$, and linearity on every finite $R$-linear combination of words. Such combinations exhaust $B$ because $P$ generates it as an $R$-algebra. Therefore $t(1_C)=\varepsilon_B=1_A$.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text:
We prove for every $b\in B$ the identity
$$E(b):\quad\langle b,cc'\rangle=\sum\langle b_1,c\rangle\langle b_2,c'\rangle\quad(c,c'\in C).$$
It holds on scalars because $r(1_B)=\varepsilon_C$ and $\varepsilon_C$ is multiplicative. On $p\in P$ it is exactly the assumed condition, using $\Delta_Bp=p\otimes1+1\otimes p$. It is closed under addition and scalar multiplication by linearity of $r$ and $\Delta_B$. If $E(x),E(y)$ hold, use $r(xy)=r(x)*r(y)$ and $\Delta_C(cc')=\sum c_1c'_1\otimes c_2c'_2$. Then
$$\langle xy,cc'\rangle=\sum\langle x,c_1c'_1\rangle\langle y,c_2c'_2\rangle=\sum\langle x_1,c_1\rangle\langle x_2,c'_1\rangle\langle y_1,c_2\rangle\langle y_2,c'_2\rangle=\sum\langle x_1y_1,c\rangle\langle x_2y_2,c'\rangle.$$
The middle factors commute in $R$, and the last equality uses convolution twice; $\Delta_B(xy)=\sum x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$. Thus $E(xy)$ holds. Induction on word length followed by linearity proves $E(b)$ for all $b$. It says exactly $t(cc')(b)=(t(c)t(c'))(b)$; hence $t$ is an algebra map as well as the coalgebra map of Step 6. The only convolution facts used are the formula and associativity of [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra].

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: Such a bialgebra map $t:C\to A$ respects antipodes by the following explicit inverse argument. In the associative convolution algebra $\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A)$ of [lem-sfb-convolution-linear-map-algebra], with unit $e=\eta_A\varepsilon_C$, put $u=t\circ S_C$ and $v=S_A\circ t$. Multiplicativity and unit compatibility of $t$ give $u*t=t*u=e$ by the two antipode identities in $C$. The coalgebra and counit compatibilities give $v*t=t*v=e$ by the two antipode identities in $A$. Therefore $u=u*(t*v)=(u*t)*v=v$. Thus $t$ is a Hopf map. Conversely, if $t_r$ is a Hopf map, its multiplicativity gives $\langle p,cc'\rangle=(t_r(c)t_r(c'))(p)$; inserting $\Delta_Bp=p\otimes1+1\otimes p$ and $r(1_B)=\varepsilon_C$ yields exactly the required generator identity. This proves both directions.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text: Given a Hopf map $t:C\to A$, define $r(b)(c)=t(c)(b)$. This is $R$-linear in both variables. Evaluating $\Delta_A t(c)=(t\otimes t)\Delta_Cc$ at $(b,b')$ gives $r(bb')(c)=\sum r(b)(c_1)r(b')(c_2)$; evaluating counit compatibility gives $r(1_B)(c)=\varepsilon_C(c)$. Hence $r$ is a unital convolution-algebra map. Its generator identity follows from multiplicativity of $t$ as in Step 9. Transposition twice leaves every value $\langle b,c\rangle$ unchanged, so it is an inverse correspondence, and equality on all $b,c$ proves uniqueness.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222–223; Definition 3.3 and discussion 3.4, pp.65–66. Explicit finite-free ring and generator-pairing calculations supplied by Q134.

proof.text:
For a Hopf map $\beta:B'\to B$, replacing the pairing by $\langle\beta(b'),c\rangle$ sends $r$ to $r\circ\beta$ and $t$ to $\beta^\vee\circ t$; for $\gamma:C'\to C$, replacing it by $\langle b,\gamma(c')\rangle$ sends $r(b)$ to $r(b)\circ\gamma$ and $t$ to $t\circ\gamma$. Thus transposition is natural wherever these data are defined. For any $R\to T$, the scalar-extended pairing is
$$\langle u\otimes b,v\otimes c\rangle_T=uv\langle b,c\rangle.$$
Bilinearity makes it balanced. Every convolution, unit, coproduct and antipode formula above evaluated on pure tensors is its old value multiplied by the participating scalars; pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Under $\theta$ of Step 5, the transposed map is therefore exactly $T\otimes t$, and the other transpose is the map into $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T\otimes C,T)$ specified by this pairing. This asserts no isomorphism $T\otimes C^*\cong(T\otimes C)^*$ for infinite $C$. The generator condition persists for $1\otimes P$, which still generates $T\otimes B$. Successive scalar extensions multiply the same scalars, so all comparison formulas are compatible with composition.
